# Phase Three — Thirty-Two Further Revelations

> After the first map, another map appears beneath the floor; the Awtsmoos creates the question and the truthful answer more.  
> Awtsmoos.com should not merely play a film that happens once; it should preserve the language from which endless films can dance.

This final critique goes beyond the previous pass and tightens implementation and proof.

1. Add `projectId` and `seed` to the canonical document for reproducible identity and procedural generation.
2. Give every scene an explicit `start`, `duration`, and derived `end`; never infer scene order solely from array position.
3. Keep a canonical `dimensions` object so aspect ratio is not hidden inside renderer state.
4. Add `background` as scene data so tutorials and infographics can render cleanly without fake giant rectangles.
5. Give layers `start` and `duration` relative to their scene, enabling entrance/exit choreography.
6. Add normalized transforms with position/scale/rotation/opacity fields shared across visual kinds.
7. Add text alignment/font-weight/size as portable style fields while leaving renderer-specific typography in `options`.
8. Define shape primitives including rect, circle, line, arrow, polygon, star, and path.
9. Define character intents separately from raw drawing implementation so Canvas silhouettes can later upgrade to Animator rigs/Three humans.
10. Model particles by named presets plus seed, count, spread, speed, gravity, lifespan, and palette intent.
11. Treat charts as semantic data layers, not collections of hand-authored rectangles, so AI can generate educational visuals robustly.
12. Treat tutorial pointers/callouts as semantic layers with `targetId`, label, and emphasis style.
13. Add camera layers/cues even to 2D: pan/zoom/rotate viewport transforms can prove shot language without fake 3D.
14. Store transitions at scene boundaries and let renderer profiles choose implementations.
15. Add `tags` to scenes and layers for AI/editor search, feature coverage, and semantic grouping.
16. Build a `MovieCoverage` helper so tests can count real requested capabilities rather than inspecting fixture text.
17. Build interpolation as a small pure helper to keep evaluator modules below 120 lines.
18. Use easing names with a stable small built-in set; unsupported custom easing should not execute arbitrary code.
19. Clamp timeline sampling to valid ranges and define end-frame behavior precisely.
20. Pause playback when the document changes to avoid stale requestAnimationFrame state.
21. Render scene-local coordinates into a logical fixed-size canvas, then scale via CSS for responsive mobile quality.
22. Use `devicePixelRatio` caps to balance sharpness and mobile performance.
23. Keep timeline scrubber touch-friendly and expose current time numerically for precise testing.
24. Build a scene-strip summary for phone rather than a desktop multitrack editor in the first unified shell.
25. Add an AI textarea/button that accepts JSON intent initially; free-text model integration can call the same compiler later.
26. Expose a `loadMovie(document)` API on Awtsmoos Studio so every existing app can embed or hand off projects.
27. Expose `getCapabilityProfile()` from each adapter to make unsupported features visible before render.
28. Give the proof movie at least twelve scenes and at least six distinct camera shot/motion patterns.
29. Require proof coverage across character, text, shape, path/arrow, particles, chart/infographic, tutorial callout, and 3D-intent layers.
30. Make at least one scene intentionally hybrid, with 3D-intent world/character layers plus 2D labels/tutorial overlays.
31. Verify reduced-motion behavior by allowing UI animation to collapse without altering movie playback semantics.
32. Record exact limitations honestly: a browser Canvas proof of a `mesh`/`world3d` intent is a fallback visualization unless the Three adapter actually runs it.

## Final Architecture Refinement

The canonical document is renderer-neutral and semantic. The first Awtsmoos Studio renderer is a deterministic Canvas implementation that can execute broad 2D semantics and visibly represent 3D intents with perspective-style fallbacks. A capability profile clearly labels native vs fallback behavior. Existing mature 3D and NLE apps attach through adapters rather than being reimplemented. This is more honest and more extensible than claiming one new renderer suddenly replaces years of Animator/Nesher functionality.

## Completion Standard Refined

A valid completion state must show:

- reusable movie modules in procedural core;
- reusable declarative Awtsmoos UI library;
- a functioning new Awtsmoos Studio shell;
- adapters/profiles for the five known studio/editor surfaces where imports are safe;
- exact 180-second canonical proof document;
- broad feature and camera coverage assertions;
- deterministic preview playback and scrubbing;
- mobile browser proof;
- no uncaught browser-console errors from the new app;
- syntax/tests passing;
- source headers/tabs/line limits audited;
- exported media duration verified if a real export path can be completed from available local tooling;
- remaining limitations written explicitly instead of hidden.
